newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean stocks close lower as blue chips fall.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean stocks close lower as blue chips fall.

text.p: South Korean stocks closed lower on Tuesday as blue chips fell, but paper and pharmaceutical makers rose on bargain hunting, brokers said.
The composite index ended 3.30 points lower at 701.57.
"Blue chips fell as institutional investors stayed on the sidelines," said Kim Young-bum of Seoul Securities.
Affiliates of the troubled Jinro Group fell on concerns that the group's plan to sell some property and affiliates had made little progress, brokers said.
Monday's surge on Wall Street was ignored and had little impact on the local market, they said.
The Dow industrials rose two percent to an all-time high of 7214 on Monday.
Nam Han Paper went limit-up to 6,230 won by rising 460 won and Shin Ho Paper also closed limit-up at 6,920 won by gaining 510 won.

Jinro Ltd fell 560 won to its limit of 6,450 and Jinro Industries lost 300 won to 3,980. The Jinro Group has reported no progress yet since it announced last month a plan to raise about 1.2 trillion won to pay back debt.
OB Brewery announced a plan to absorb its sister firm Doo San Beverage on October 1.

Trading in shares of the two companies was suspended for the afternoon session following the announcement. OB Brewery last traded at 31,000 won, down 2,300 won on the day, and Doo San at 34,700 won, up 900 won.
Brokers said OB Brewery shares would fall on Wednesday because the stock's price has recently risen sharply on expectations for a similar plan.
"The merger plan has now faded as a factor for the stock. I think investors will prefer to take profit now," said Koh Soon-shik of LG Securities.
